acf50682ee: Starting from what the system is for, this teardown goes through mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics of Naruto Mobile's growth and economy: how two kinds of fairness coexist across modes, where account power pays off, and how eight recruitment channels serve different budgets. Rules are taken from the live game in October–November 2026, and key claims are tagged by type of evidence.
f942f43723: Face-value gap, same S-rank ninja25×Premium recruit ≈ ¥5,040 vs. Legendary pass ¥198
10dc9151e0: Power modes5Leaderboard, Peak Duel and three guild modes
5a3e650034: Ways to control new-ninja strength3Stat normalisation, bans, mode eligibility
adc8734925: Magic-resist gap on my account3080Level requirement met, stuck on the stat threshold
8ad8b94a40: Fighting games keep players with fairness; free-to-play games earn money from paid advantages. Naruto Mobile does not pick one side for the whole game. Instead, two kinds of fairness coexist mode by mode: ranked duels mask combat stats, so skill and ninja roster decide; account power pays off in the server leaderboard, guild modes and the Peak Duel.
0532ef9701: What power buysBeing seen and being neededThe server power leaderboard sets your ranking and gives the top five a points bonus in Peak Duel qualifiers; Fortress, Heaven & Earth Battlefield and Guild Clash turn individual power into guild results. Points League still exists but is no longer what power players care about.
d2baceb89b: Two playstylesHeavily overlapping, not two campsThe Peak Duel demands power, real-time skill and a deep roster at once: 3v3 with bans before picks, and S/A/B ninjas you have used cannot return in later rounds. Most invested players do both.
fe76538f0a: Strength controlMode eligibility on top of normalisation and bansAs of November, the tenth-anniversary limited S-rank “Naruto Uzumaki · Sasuke Uchiha” and “Naruto Uzumaki · Jiraiya” cannot be used in the four power modes, so the impact of a new release stays in ranked duels first.
6fd94fd772: Acquisition channelsTiered by certaintyFor the same S-rank tier, Premium Recruit costs about ¥5,040 at face value, while the Legendary pass costs ¥198 plus a season of activity. Most of the gap is absorbed by free gold and time, so it is not a price difference for the same product.
be1593636d: Three growth lines, five places to pay off
c31e53fe81: Ninja acquisition, ninja upgrades and account power produce two things: “do you own it” and “how strong are you”. Ranked duels only care about ownership, the leaderboard and guild modes care about strength, and the Peak Duel needs both.
0c87eccc11: Ninjas have the widest reach of any item, but they are not the only ones that cross over. Summons and scrolls affect tactics in ranked duels and also have stat upgrades; outfits provide both expression and stats.
7d00cbd738: Shows individual ranking; the top five by power get a 30% / 20% / 10% points bonus in Peak Duel qualifiers
bfcdd0117f: Every five weeks: server final on Friday, cross-server on Saturday
0e3322c12d: Players far below in power cannot challenge; 3v3 with bans before picks, used S/A/B ninjas cannot return; on a forfeit the higher-power player advances
2c57546550: Longer win streaks score more; guild points decide who holds the fortress
a84fd38de8: Requires ten members to pray that day; fighting with the random “recommended ninja” grants an attack bonus
1d9d608f2c: Top 16 guilds by power may enter; relay battles, each side bans three ninjas
143e8c5fff: Rules are from the in-game rule pages in November 2026. Low interest in Points League is an observation from my own server and may not hold everywhere.
83d8781188: For the same S-rank tier, the two routes differ by about 25× at face value. Face value, cash, time and risk have to be compared separately; otherwise two different ways of paying get misread as price discrimination on one product.
3007f78fd0: Only known after subtracting stored gold, tickets and free income; can be far below face value
a7ccd576d1: Minus coupon balance; four ¥50 monthly top-ups cover it exactly
fa9e21244f: Depends on how fast gold accumulates and on luck
80337c86e5: A season of activity to reach the reward level, or buy levels with coupons
1989f4426f: Pull count is random; other shards and materials along the way
36ad1d3e0c: Fixed reward, but only that season's ninja
bab3529b3d: Full-unlock cost“About 300 pulls” is a player estimate, not a guaranteeThe game only publishes per-category shard rates and a guaranteed S shard every ten pulls. The cost of a full ninja needs a conditional model: starting shards, shards per pull, event top-ups and exchanges, solved for the minimum number of pulls, reported as both a median and a high percentile.
fcce98495d: Monthly budgetFour ¥50 top-ups pay for a season passThe ¥50 tier yields 565 coupons; four months give 2,260, leaving 280 after the 1,980-coupon Legendary pass. Buying one more 1,980-coupon ninja in the same window leaves you 1,700 short.
7c927d4836: Spending capsMoney speeds you up, within limitsAll VIP 12 perks are purchase counts; buying each weekly-limited power bundle once costs about ¥600. Level gates, daily purchase limits and weekly limits together set the fastest possible pace.
0485ce9f80: Growth bottleneckLevel is enough, magic resist is 3080 shortMy level-161 account meets the level requirement for level-160 accessories, but magic resist is 46,341 against 49,421. Each tier raises the threshold by about 10%; buying resources that are not the bottleneck does not move progress.
150a676a38: Every conclusion is written as a chain: which rule → what players do because of it → what they feel → which goal it serves. The full text has 14; six are shown here. The behaviour and experience columns lack backend data and are inferred from the mechanics.

d745df3420: Challenge: wins and losses feel like your own

6d7338fd0e: Exclusivity for owners, deprivation for everyone else
6b5d7bdb3a: Two flywheels meet at the ninja. The competitive flywheel is driven by new ninjas, so demand comes in pulses; the power flywheel is driven by the social standing that the leaderboard and guild modes give, so investment is continuous. The Peak Duel draws on both.
fcfb15de91: ExperienceFour motivations interwovenCompetitive expression, rank and growth, guild belonging and character affection. Guild modes make fellowship the strongest retention experience on the power side: Wednesday battlefield, Saturday fortress, personal growth gets an audience and teammates. The cost is attendance pressure at fixed times.
e3f95efa69: ComparisonYiren zhi Xia: only sourced comparisonsSame studio, also a fighting game; the public line is that PvP ignores level and gear, but tests showed a “constellation” upgrade that can be unlocked early with money. The comparison only covers which modes paid assets affect and does not predict its revenue mix.
0ab61cdc8f: Small changes that first verify whether a problem exists come before changes to resource income. None of the three touches the paywall itself (coupon ninjas require payment); they only deal with the information and experience costs it creates.
ffea099dbc: Make Premium Recruit rules and budget information transparent
35a2c28f66: Players cannot tell category shard rates, the ten-pull guarantee and full-unlock cost apart; the same game already shows a live luck meter in Wish Treasure
47b91dec14: Some players stop once they hit a guaranteed reward, so revenue per banner may drop
49078730cd: Training access to paid ninjas you do not own
674bd8f2d9: Without the ninja, there is no way to practise against it
273e30653d: Upgrade systems keep stacking, so returning players on old servers fall far behind
098e58a938: Veterans may feel it is unfair; subsidies may go to unintended uses
9e42420646: Roster pressure from high-rank bans; how long the mode restrictions on specific ninjas last
24d9351b47: Players with a thin roster may run out of usable ninjas at high ranks
ff99bc5625: Proposal ① is validated in two steps. First a small usability test: can players tell category shard rates from full-unlock odds, and can they judge whether their budget covers a guaranteed reward? Only then look at live support tickets and spending by budget tier, splitting any revenue change into earlier spending, delayed spending and real change. Full-unlock progress is shown only if a hard full-unlock guarantee actually exists; player estimates are never presented as a guarantee.
df845283de: Catch-up has to account for a moving target: time to catch up is roughly T = D ÷ (a − b), where D is the starting gap, a the player's effective daily growth and b the target's daily growth; you only catch up if a > b. Subsidies go only to materials identified as bottlenecks.

5fd086fbf6: Battlegrounds has no card collection: eight players share one minion pool, and results depend almost entirely on resource decisions within a match. This teardown looks at a single match through mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics: how gold becomes a board, how the shared pool sets the cost of finding cards, and how health limits when to invest. Season 14, October 2026; I have played the mode for 501 hours, with a past-season best above 10,000 rating.
88fffdf2ed: Upgrades' share of base gold, turns 1–1046%33 of 72 gold on the baseline route
bed3add98b: Hit rate per refresh after 2 target copies are taken15→8%Static pool example
0ad88768cf: Earliest elimination under damage capsTurn 530 health, no armour
a9fae6da3a: Hero-choice coverage with the season pass36→60%2 options to 4, under stated assumptions
c0f014c307: The gap between strong and weak boards has to open up for placements to mean anything; if it opens too early, most players run out of meaningful choices. Most key decisions in a match trade “cash in now” against “wait for better supply”.
92e8318f4b: Finding 1Same base income, different buying powerGold starts at 3, rises by 1 a turn and caps at 10 from turn 8 for everyone; economy engines like Trade Prince Gallywix, selling and discounts change what you can actually spend. No interest and no win-streak bonus cut the direct link from winning to more gold.
18abcd00bb: Finding 2Copy counts set search cost, not triple oddsA tier-6 minion has 7 copies; a triple takes 3 and leaves 4. Whether you find it depends on the size of the visible pool and the number of shop slots.
c3ee111f7a: Finding 3The shared pool cuts both waysIt can stop the leader from making a second golden copy, and it can also stop players behind from copying the leader's board. It is not a reliable catch-up mechanism.
96d052b034: Finding 4Payment buys hero-choice coverage, not win rateThe season pass expands the starting hero choice from 2 to 4 without changing any in-match rule after you pick. I have always played free with 2 options and still reached over 10,000 in a past season.
18234213af: Rules are from Season 14 patch notes and the in-game UI; curves and probabilities are my own calculations under stated assumptions, mathematical examples of how the variables relate, not real match statistics.
1c86bfb3ab: Upgrading buys future supply. On a baseline of upgrading on turns 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10, 33 of the 72 base gold in turns 1–10 go to upgrades (45.8%), and none of the five upgrade turns leaves enough to buy another minion. Health is the deposit on this deal.
fa31b957a7: Fewer copies, bigger share per triple. A tier-6 minion has 7 copies; a triple takes 42.9% but leaves 4, so a second player can still triple it.
0f4010b1fe: Looking only at the denominator is misleading. Hit rate per refresh is p = 1 − C(N−m, k) ÷ C(N, k). If the pool grows and the shop gains a slot, the rate can go up (15.28% → 15.84%); if someone takes two of your targets, it drops from 15.28% to 8.04%, nearly halving your search efficiency.
4a62c230a9: Triples drive the snowball, and four mechanisms limit it at different stages; not all of them help the player who is behind.
ac327d4a01: Positive feedback runs through the board. No interest, damage caps and triple rewards only one tier up all slow down how fast a lead grows; the shared pool cuts both ways.
58666d2439: Health budgetArmour converts into extra turns you can waitSolo damage caps are 5 on turns 1–3, 10 on turns 4–7 and 15 from turn 8, removed once you reach the top four. The cap only guarantees how fast you can be knocked out at most; it does not guarantee you survive to any particular power spike.
f690d9cf09: Dark giftsWaiting only pays if survival odds are high3 gold each, from turn 3, at most once per turn and three times per match, with options improving each turn. If using one now is worth 100 and waiting until a target turn is worth 140, waiting needs a survival chance above 71.4%.
1f0e53ae48: Price testWhat if upgrade costs were linearChanging upgrade prices to 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 changes both the shape and the total (42 → 45). Taken apart, the +2 on tier 6 leaves you 1 gold short on turn 10; the claim that it would remove the tier-4-to-5 decision point does not hold, because the tier-5 base price is unchanged.
80711f5476: The core economy is solid; the problems are information transparency, the learning cost of season turnover, and the link between payment and ranked play. Changes that only alter what information is shown, and can first verify that the problem exists, come first.

66570427eb: Step 1Test understanding with decision questionsUsability tests with new, returning and experienced players: can they tell initial copies from current stock, say which turn an opponent record is from, and weigh both copy counts and shop slots when comparing searches?
531fdd0a73: Step 2Randomise by whole matchAll eight players in a match see the same feature. The primary metric is accuracy on post-match rule questions; guardrails include unfinished actions, performance and abnormal exits.
fcc63b3d4b: Dropped metric“Share of matches with a shared tribe” does not workWith eight players across five tribes, at least two sharing a tribe is almost certain, and sharing a tribe does not mean competing for the same pieces. Sample size is estimated after a pilot gives accuracy and response rates.
